children: in the third quarter are a good sign for the semiconductor foundry giant's fourth quarter, Wedbush Securities said.
Shares rose 1.4% in premarket trading on Friday.

"While TSMC has consistently delivered modest upside vs. its outlook through the AI boom, we would note this result represents a slightly larger than typical beat (for instance upside last quarter totaled ~1%)," Wedbush analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. "The exchange rate was essentially in-line with the 32.0 TWD/USD embedded in the outlook. With revenue ahead of the range and FX neutral, we would expect GMs likely at least will meet the 66% midpoint of TSMC’s 65% to 67% guide (vs. our 66.0% and consensus at 66.5%) and more likely exceed our estimate given better utilization rates (and TSMC's tendency to guide conservatively)."

"Given TSMC’s near monopoly position in cutting edge fabrication with all major AI paths currently reliant on TSMC, we continue to see [the stock] as one of the best and safest ways to invest in a future we believe will be dominated by AI," Bryson added. Bryson has an Outperform rating on Taiwan Semiconductor and a NT$3,000 price target on the stock.

Taiwan Semiconductor, the world’s largest contract chipmaker, reported record third revenue of NT$1.49T ($46.71B), up 50% year-over-year, as surging demand for AI applications continued to drive semiconductor sales. Revenue exceeded the LSEG SmartEstimate of NT$1.46T and the company's own guidance of $44.6B to $45.8B.
Taiwan Semiconductor is scheduled to release its full third-quarter financial results and provide updated guidance on Oct. 15.

title: Taiwan Semiconductor's strong Q3 sales a positive sign for Q4, Wedbush says
